subtitles.text:
Ten miles from the ocean.
Never touched the sand.

Mom worked three jobs.
She never complained.

We didn't go to the beach.
The beach wasn't for us.
My father died when I was seven.

Shot in a ditch
with seventeen dollars.

He loved us.
He loved the street more.

Got arrested as a kid.
Stupid stuff.

Then at twenty-one,
I was framed.

Learned to code
on a broken computer.

Interview goes great.
Then: background check.

Door after door
slams shut.
I'm drowning.

I built an app.
Called it No Sand Beach.

Rewrote my background.
Gave myself a fake degree.

Got the job.
Got the office.
Got the view.

I forgot my mother's laugh.
I forgot my brother's voice.

I was becoming
a stranger to myself.

Dad appeared as a glitch:
"You're killing her by becoming someone else."

I collapsed on the office floor.
Mom held my hand.
Marcus came.
We reconciled.

I deleted it. Line by line.
Got my real memories back.

Touched the sand.

Love isn't a subscription.
It's the ground under your feet.

You don't have to erase who you are.
